tasks.short: Identify possible compliance breaches and decide which need investigation.

steps.what: Collect complaints, control exceptions and relevant transaction records.
Read case documents against relevant obligations and policies.

loop.input: Case evidence and approved, versioned obligations and policies.
loop.output: Possible issues with source passages, contradictions and missing evidence.
loop.check: Verify source references and versions; the officer checks material claims before investigation decisions.
loop.stop: One pass and one correction per case; unresolved conflicts return to the officer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative complaints and case documents describe possible breaches in varied language.

steps.what: Check dates, thresholds and transaction patterns in exported records.
Decide whether the evidence warrants follow-up, investigation or closure.
Record the decision and assign follow-up with a deadline.

tasks.design: A connector on the {DATA_PLATFORM} gathers permitted evidence from the {ERP}, {HELPDESK} and {WORKFLOW}, then runs approved control rules. A bounded reading loop compares narrative evidence with versioned obligations in the {DOCS}; the compliance officer decides the disposition before the {WORKFLOW} assigns follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence sits across systems, and narrative allegations rarely fit fixed rules. Bespoke connectors and evidence tracing were costly to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding can reduce connector and rule-engine development effort. Bounded document reading can produce source-linked drafts; legal judgement remains necessary.
tasks.still_hard: Contradictory evidence, privilege, sensitive allegations and uncertain legal applicability. Access controls and false-negative testing remain substantial work.
tasks.human_edge: Weigh credibility, context and proportionality, and distinguish a weak signal from a serious breach.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from collecting files to reviewing evidence and choosing investigation priorities. With delegated authority, the officer can redirect investigation capacity across controls.

reach.task: Triage suspicious payment patterns alongside compliance allegations.
reach.learn: Evidence preservation, fraud indicators and the limits of pattern-based suspicion.

reach.task: Assess the financial exposure of recurring control exceptions.
reach.learn: Exposure estimation and risk appetite thresholds.

evidence.claim: Structured thresholds and deadlines support deterministic checks; narrative allegations still require judgement.
Shift Technology documents fraud screening in insurance; this supports screening feasibility, not general compliance accuracy.
GDPR Article 22 requires a separate assessment when automation makes legally or similarly significant decisions about people.
Dutch requirements include a mandatory DPIA list covering specified fraud-prevention and monitoring processing; national rules elsewhere vary.

assumptions: A typical mid-size company has digital case records and some spreadsheet-based checks.
Flags inform investigation decisions and do not automatically impose sanctions.
The judgement prior is retained; record gathering and explicit checks are more automatable.
Build ranges are planning estimates for one case queue and a limited connector set, not sourced performance claims.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; purpose and deployment determine relevant duties. Employee consultation follows national rules.
unknowns: Available case systems, interfaces and evidence permissions.
Applicable obligations, sector rules and approved control thresholds.
Whether cases involve employees, customers or legally significant decisions.
Investigation authority, escalation thresholds and retention requirements.
Required consultation, DPIA and access-approval lead times.
research_questions: Which existing configurations can replace spreadsheet checks?
How well does source-linked triage perform on independently labelled historic cases?
Which exceptions reveal missing data rather than possible non-compliance?
new_work: Review narrative issue drafts and unresolved contradictions.
Maintain versioned control rules and obligation mappings.
Monitor missed issues and excessive flags using sampled cases.
Maintain connectors, permissions and evidence retention.

tasks.short: Track regulatory and industry developments and assess their relevance.

steps.what: Scan subscribed alerts and newsletters for new developments.
Read official notices, proposals and industry guidance.

loop.input: Retrieved source documents from the approved source register.
loop.output: Source-linked changes, proposal status, affected activities and stated effective dates.
loop.check: Validate every reference and quoted date against retrieved text; inspect material changes in the source.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per document; unreadable or conflicting sources enter a manual queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Notices describe changes in prose and use inconsistent document structures.

steps.what: Record changes, remove duplicates and note expected dates.
Assess applicability, uncertainty and whether a policy review is needed.
Share relevant extracts and review recommendations with affected teams.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} collects subscribed alerts and maintains a deduplicated change register, with source-linked summaries stored in the {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop prepares the reading brief, and the compliance officer records applicability decisions before approved findings appear in the {BI} and trigger targeted notifications.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source formats and update schedules vary. Collecting alerts was feasible, but useful summaries and applicability checks required sustained reading.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing subscriptions and scheduled retrieval handle collection. Bounded extraction and faster connector development reduce preparation effort without resolving legal uncertainty.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing proposals from binding requirements, finding amendments and judging effects on specific activities. Restricted sources and incomplete coverage remain problems.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise which developments matter to the business and when uncertain guidance warrants specialist advice.

ambition.what: Monthly regulatory horizon clinic for finance process owners

tasks.altitude: The week includes less alert scanning and more focused reading and discussion with process owners. No new decision rights arise automatically; the officer can recommend earlier reviews.

reach.task: Translate upcoming regulatory changes into budget and resource implications.
reach.learn: Budget cycles, implementation costs and dependencies between finance processes.

reach.task: Assess which regulatory developments require filing-process changes.
reach.learn: Filing calendars, tax-specific applicability and evidence requirements.

evidence.claim: Subscriptions, duplicate detection and source registers can automate collection without deciding legal applicability.
Veeva RIM tracks registrations and submissions in a regulated sector; it does not establish generic horizon-scanning capability.
A documented report failure involving nonexistent sources supports checking generated references against retrieved originals.

assumptions: The source set includes public official material and authorised subscriptions.
The gathering prior is retained, but professional learning and applicability assessment remain human work.
Unreviewed summaries carry draft status and do not amend the obligation register.
Build ranges are planning estimates for a limited source set.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Internal confidential context is excluded from public-source retrieval.
unknowns: Relevant jurisdictions, sectors, business activities and source subscriptions.
Source licensing and permitted retrieval methods.
Who can approve obligation-register changes.
Whether internal business context may enter the reading service.
Required source languages and update cadence.
research_questions: Which official sources offer feeds or stable retrieval interfaces?
How often are material developments missed by the existing source set?
Can date and legal-status extraction distinguish proposals, adoption and commencement reliably?
new_work: Maintain the source register and repair failed retrievals.
Check material summaries against original text.
Resolve duplicate, amended and conflicting notices.
Review source coverage and retire low-value alerts.

tasks.short: Help auditors obtain evidence, understand controls and resolve compliance review questions.

steps.what: Clarify audit requests, scope, deadlines and permitted disclosures.
Request missing evidence from control owners and track responses.
Retrieve transaction records and control results for requested periods.
Check evidence completeness and prepare explanations with an evidence index.

loop.input: Agreed requests and authorised evidence with identifiers and reporting periods.
loop.output: Draft explanations linked to an evidence index, with explicit gaps and limitations.
loop.check: Code checks identifiers, periods and totals; the officer verifies each material explanation.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair per request; unsupported answers remain marked as gaps.
loop.why_not_simpler: Auditors ask varied narrative questions that require explanations across several documents.

steps.what: Approve disclosure and release the evidence package to the auditor.
Explain control operation, discuss gaps and agree follow-up.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} tracks agreed requests and gathers authorised evidence through connectors to the {ERP} and {DOCS}. A deterministic package builder creates the index, while a bounded loop drafts source-linked explanations; the compliance officer approves each release and handles auditor discussions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrive in different formats, evidence ownership is scattered, and disclosure needs judgement. Standard trackers helped coordination but did not assemble defensible answers.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured request workflows and reusable extraction code handle much of the preparation. Bounded drafting can join evidence into explanations with references for review.
tasks.still_hard: Evidence quality, privilege, disclosure boundaries and contested findings. Explaining how controls work in practice still requires knowledgeable people.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust with auditors, acknowledge weaknesses candidly and challenge conclusions using defensible evidence.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from chasing attachments to resolving evidence gaps and preparing control owners for review. The officer gains no automatic authority over audit findings or remediation budgets.

reach.task: Reconcile audit extracts to financial control totals.
reach.learn: Ledger reconciliation, period cut-offs and accounting evidence.

reach.task: Assess whether evidence demonstrates control operation.
reach.learn: Sampling, audit assertions and independence boundaries.

evidence.claim: Request tracking, evidence indexing and period-based extraction support deterministic preparation.
A documented generated-report failure supports verifying citations before releasing audit explanations.
DNB reported documentation and monitoring weaknesses in insurer AI use; that evidence is sector-specific.

assumptions: The compliance officer supports audits rather than independently determining the auditor's findings.
Audits commonly combine calls, mailbox coordination, system extracts and document packages.
The human-task prior applies to scope and explanation; preparation has substantial automation potential.
Build ranges are planning estimates for one audit process and a limited evidence set.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Employee-related evidence and consultation require assessment under national rules.
unknowns: Auditor access arrangements and permitted disclosure channels.
Evidence locations, owners, retention and privilege restrictions.
Who has authority to release each evidence category.
Whether extraction can reproduce historical records and control totals.
Required employee consultation and access approvals.
research_questions: Which evidence requests recur enough to support fixed extraction templates?
Can packages preserve reproducible snapshots and source versions?
Which explanations require interviews because documentary evidence is insufficient?
new_work: Review draft explanations and evidence gaps.
Approve releases and check disclosure permissions.
Maintain extraction templates and evidence-owner mappings.
Test package completeness and manage access expiry.

tasks.short: Verify that policies are documented, operating and communicated to affected people.

steps.what: Compare applicable obligations with the policy register and document versions.

loop.input: Approved obligations, policy text, document versions and prior mappings.
loop.output: Suggested coverage links with quoted passages and possible gaps.
loop.check: Validate document versions and references; the officer confirms coverage before accepting mappings.
loop.stop: One comparison and one repair per policy; ambiguous obligations remain unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Policies express obligations in different wording, and a keyword match cannot establish coverage.

steps.what: Ask policy owners for implementation evidence and missing documentation.
Inspect control records for evidence that procedures operate.
Check publication, acknowledgements and required training completion.
Resolve conflicting evidence with policy owners and decide whether gaps remain.
Record assurance status and assign corrective actions with deadlines.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} holds obligation, policy and control links, requests evidence and tracks corrective actions. Connectors check version and completion records from the {DOCS}, {ERP}, {LMS} and {HCM}; a bounded reading loop suggests policy coverage, while the compliance officer signs assurance decisions before status reaches the {BI}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy documents, operating evidence and communication records use different identifiers and owners. Document existence was easier to verify than effective implementation.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured records and reminders handle ownership and deadlines. Faster integration development and bounded text comparison reduce reconciliation effort.
tasks.still_hard: Proving that procedures work, interpreting partial coverage and reaching contractors or staff outside standard records. Completion data does not establish understanding.
tasks.human_edge: Test whether a policy changes real behaviour and challenge reassuring paperwork that lacks operating evidence.

ambition.what: Monthly prioritisation of policy implementation gaps

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from collecting acknowledgements to testing weak controls and discussing practical fixes. With delegated authority, the officer can set corrective-action priorities; policy approval remains with its authorised owner.

reach.task: Test control effectiveness using targeted evidence samples.
reach.learn: Sampling design and the difference between control design and operating effectiveness.

reach.task: Build reliable policy coverage and remediation reporting.
reach.learn: Data lineage, denominator definitions and access-controlled reporting.

evidence.claim: Version checks, owner reminders and completion reconciliation support deterministic automation; effective implementation still needs evidence assessment.
Dutch works-council law includes consent rights for specified employee-data and monitoring arrangements; national rules elsewhere vary.
Employee evaluation can fall within the EU AI Act's high-risk categories; administrative completion tracking alone does not establish that classification.
DNB documented weaknesses in insurer AI documentation and monitoring, supporting checks beyond the existence of policy documents.

assumptions: Policies have identifiable owners and approved versions, although cross-system mappings may be incomplete.
The document-heavy prior is retained; the decomposition gives more time to operating-evidence checks than document formatting.
Completion checks support assurance and do not score employee performance.
Build ranges are planning estimates for one policy family and a limited system set.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Consultation, monitoring and employment requirements depend on national rules.
unknowns: Policy ownership, approved obligation mappings and evidence standards.
Interfaces and identifiers shared by employee, training and policy records.
Whether contractors and other affected groups appear in scope records.
Whether use of individual completion records constitutes employee monitoring.
Required consultation, privacy assessment and access-approval times.
Authority to accept residual gaps and assign remediation.
research_questions: Which existing workflow and learning configurations already provide the required records?
Which controls can be tested from system evidence, and which require observation or interviews?
How accurately do proposed coverage links distinguish partial coverage from full coverage?
new_work: Investigate missing evidence and conflicting completion records.
Maintain policy ownership, scope mappings and test definitions.
Sample operating controls and review access to employee-level records.
Track overdue remediation and verify closure evidence.

role.altitude: The compliance officer spends more of the week interpreting evidence, discussing weak controls and prioritising follow-up. New investigation or remediation rights require explicit delegation; automation alone grants none.
reach: Support fraud analysts with source-linked case triage.
Help accountants produce reproducible audit evidence.
Work with financial managers on regulatory implementation costs.
Partner with internal auditors on control effectiveness testing.
Help business intelligence analysts define trustworthy assurance measures.
skills_to_grow: Translate obligations into testable controls without overstating certainty.
Assess evidence quality, lineage and missing-data risks.
Review source-linked model drafts and measure errors using independent samples.
Design proportionate access, retention and disclosure controls.
Use financial materiality and risk appetite to prioritise investigations.
Apply GDPR, relevant EU AI Act duties and national consultation rules to the actual deployment.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a recurring compliance readiness service that connects regulatory changes, policy gaps, case signals and audit evidence. Use it to recommend earlier corrective action and direct authorised investigation capacity toward the most consequential weaknesses.
